subject: Small-batch strategy + budget fallbacks — post-call decision brief
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinnaclepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Small-batch strategy + budget fallbacks — post-call decision brief

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete options we discussed so the team can align on next steps. Please confirm anything I mis-stated.

Key pains you called out:
- Monthly token spend is the gating constraint (target ceiling: ~$8k/month for pilot).
- Peak traffic spikes (rule-of-thumb: 3x baseline during promos) cause large cost variability and occasional latency spikes.
- Need predictable unit economics before committing to a full rollout; finance needs 2–4 week visibility during pilot.

Goals we agreed:
- Prove 30–45% token-cost reduction via batching + prefix/KV caching while keeping P95 latency <150ms for prioritized flows.
- Validate end-to-end cost model for 1M tokens/day baseline and a stretch 3M tokens/day scenario.
- Deliver an ops checklist plus gating criteria finance will sign off on.

Suggested levers and what we recommend for the pilot:
1) Small-batch strategy (our "mini-batching") — preserves low tail latency while improving GPU fill for cost reduction (best for short, bursty interactions).
2) Prefix / KV caching for common prompts (expected to cut incremental token generation for repeated flows by ~20–30%).
3) Model quantization + lower-cost variant for low-priority routes (fallback to higher quality model for edge cases).
4) Reserved burst slots: a small dedicated pool to reduce P95 on spikes without committing to large monthly reserved capacity.

Initial ROI framing (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline: ~100% token cost for current configuration. With a combined mini-batching + prefix cache approach we expect 30–45% reduction in billable tokens on the tested flows; quantization adds another ~10–15% in token-equivalent cost savings when acceptable for the route.
- If baseline monthly spend at pilot scale is $8k, expected pilot spend post-optimization: ~$4.5–6k (depending on adoption and cache-hit rates).

Pilot scope / deliverables (attached: pilot-scope-v1.pdf, cost-model-worksheet.xlsx):
- 6-week technical pilot, 2 phases (integration + load/ops tuning).
- Deliverables: cost model populated with your traffic shape, weekly checkpoints, final TCO readout with recommended rollout path.

Open asks / decisions for you:
- Confirm pilot budget ceiling (your note: ~$8k/month) or propose the upper bound finance will approve.
- Provide a representative 48-hour traffic sample (JSON or CSV) so we can optimize batching parameters.
- Are there any network/egress rules (VPC or on-prem certs) we should factor in?

Next steps I propose:
1) We populate the cost-model worksheet with your sample traffic (we can take this as action).
2) Signature on the pilot SOW (DocuSign link prepared) to lock the 6-week timeline.
3) Kickoff integration the week after SOW is signed; Marissa will own ops tuning and weekly cost checkpoints.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the traffic sample and confirmation on the pilot ceiling.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (overview), cost-model-worksheet.xlsx (editable)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinnaclepay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Small-batch strategy + budget fallbacks — post-call decision brief

Thanks Kimberly — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can stretch to $8k/month for the pilot but finance will require weekly visibility and a hard stop if 2-week rolling average spends > $9k.
- Engineering bandwidth is limited — we can dedicate 1 engineer (half time) to integration for the first 3 weeks. Can you scope the integration work for that velocity?
- We need an initial guardrail estimate for the worst-case (3M tokens/day) so our CFO can sign off conditionally.

Also, important: we have strict egress rules for PII flows. Anything that touches raw payment tokens must run within our VPC — is Redwood’s private deployment path / VPN tunnel feasible for the pilot?

If you can send a short worst-case cost line item and confirm VPC support, I’ll run this by finance and legal.

— Alex
Head of Product, PinnaclePay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: quick ops notes for PinnaclePay pilot

Kim — quick internal note before we reply to Alex:
- Recommend offering a 6-week pilot with a "burst reserve" config: keep a small 4x burst pool that only activates on P95 pressure to protect latency without full reserved commitment.
- Gating criteria (finance sign-off): per-1M token cost after optimizations must be <= $X. I’ll run the model with optimistic/pessimistic cache-hit assumptions in the worksheet.
- Confirm we can support VPC tunneling for the egress-sensitive routes (Rishi, can you confirm infra feasibility and any lead time?).

I can own weekly cost checkpoints and be the primary ops contact if Kimberly is ok with that.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinnaclepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Small-batch strategy + budget fallbacks — post-call decision brief

Alex — thanks, noted and appreciate the limits. Quick replies and next actions:
1) Finance guardrail: we’ll populate the cost-model worksheet with a worst-case 3M tokens/day scenario and call out the 2-week rolling average thresholds (we’ll flag where spends exceed $9k).
2) Integration scope for a single half‑time engineer: we’ll minimize required changes — server-to-server API calls, tokenization guidance, and a small client patch for prefix annotations. Expect ~8–12 engineer-hours in week 1 for integration plus 6–10 hours/week for tuning during phase 2. I’ll attach a slim integration checklist to the SOW.
3) VPC / egress-sensitive routes: Redwood supports Private deployment with VPN tunneling for the pilot; Rishi will confirm exact lead time — initial estimate: 7–10 business days to establish a tunnel and test.

If that works, next steps:
- I’ll update the cost worksheet with the three traffic scenarios (baseline / promo spike / worst-case) and share by EOD tomorrow.
- If you can approve the pilot ceiling of $8k with the $9k conditional stop, we’ll route the SOW for signature and lock the kickoff date.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-pinnaclepay (attached in related_links)

Looking forward — we’ll keep the pilot tightly instrumented so finance has the visibility they need.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
